ex.s: I had my first dictionary as a gift for my 13th birthday.
ex.t: 我的第一本词典是13岁生日时收到的礼物。

ex.s: I decided that I wanted to learn as many words as I could and started marking every entry I looked up with a pencil to measure my progress.
ex.t: 那时我决心要尽可能多地学单词，并开始用铅笔标记每一个查过的词条，以此来衡量自己的进步。

ex.s: I continued to make these pencil marks for years, and when I went off to college, I packed that dictionary in my suitcase.
ex.t: 多年来我一直做着这些铅笔标记，离家上大学时，我把那本词典装进了行李箱。

ex.t: 我感到胸口隐隐作痛。那本词典在我大学一年级结束时被偷了。

ex.s: Now I understand that although my son may be learning differently, he is still learning.
ex.t: 现在我明白，虽然儿子的学习方式可能不同，但他仍然在学习。

ex.t: 我的大学生活必需品排名

ex.t: 我就是这样开始探寻海平面的概念史的。

ex.t: 我的第一次太极拳体验

ex.s: Although not a morning person, I begin my lesson with Angela and about twenty others at a Sydney community centre courtyard at 7 am.
ex.t: 虽然不是早起的人，我还是在早上7点和安吉拉以及另外约二十人在悉尼一个社区中心的院子里开始上课。

ex.s: I would feel completely at ease doing my homework in bed, with light music on.
ex.t: 我喜欢躺在床上做作业，放着轻音乐，感觉无比自在。

ex.s: My parents urged me to get out of this so-called unhealthy habit, but their repeated requests fell on deaf ears.
ex.t: 父母劝我改掉这个所谓不健康的习惯，但他们的一再要求都被我当成了耳旁风。

ex.s: Fast forward to my first year of college.
ex.t: 快进到我大学一年级。

ex.s: My roommates would tell me to go to bed and get up early the following morning to do it instead.
ex.t: 室友们会劝我去睡觉，第二天早上早点起来再做。

ex.s: Get up early to do my homework?
ex.t: 早起做作业？

ex.s: Bent over my laptop while sitting on the bed in the corner of my room, I suddenly felt a pounding headache, and had to lie down.
ex.t: 我弓着背坐在房间角落的床上盯着笔记本电脑，突然感到一阵剧烈的头痛，不得不躺下。

ex.s: Unable to keep my eyes open, I decided I had no choice but to finish my homework the next morning.
ex.t: 我困得睁不开眼，于是决定别无选择，只能在第二天早上完成作业。

ex.s: Hardly had I written half a page when I felt a sharp pain in my chest
ex.t: 我刚写了半页，就感到胸口一阵剧痛

ex.s: I realized that years of living as a late-night person had turned my heart into an overworked engine.
ex.t: 我意识到，多年熬夜的生活已经把我的心变成了一台过度运转的发动机。

ex.s: Slowly but surely, my efforts to adjust to the new routine paid off.
ex.t: 我努力适应新作息，缓慢但稳步地见到了成效。

ex.s: I’ve discovered that if I show students how what they learn is relevant to my hobbies, they’re much more willing to make connections to their personal interests and develop their own hobbies.
ex.t: 我发现，如果我向学生展示所学内容与我的爱好的关联，他们就更愿意把知识与自己的兴趣联系起来，并培养出自己的爱好。

ex.s: No matter what subject I’m teaching, I find ways to bring my hobbies into the classroom.
ex.t: 无论教什么科目，我都会想办法把我的爱好带进课堂。

ex.s: For example, I’m a car enthusiast, so when I teach physics, I contextualize concepts with my knowledge about cars.
ex.t: 例如，我是个汽车迷，所以教物理时，我会用自己的汽车知识来让概念更具体。

ex.s: When I first brought my hobbies to my classroom, I was focused on how doing so would build engagement and help my students understand concepts in science.
ex.t: 最初把爱好带进课堂时，我关注的是这样做能如何提高参与度、帮助学生理解科学概念。

ex.s: When I let them see an aspect of my life outside of school, some students who were also interested in cars connected with me more and became more engaged in my courses.
ex.t: 当我让他们看到我校外生活的一面时，一些同样对汽车感兴趣的学生与我更有共鸣，也更投入我的课程。

ex.s: Even when I’m planning classes, I tend to think about how I can bring in my hobbies.
ex.t: 即使在我备课的时候，我也倾向于想着怎么把我的爱好带进去。

ex.s: I find that doing so energizes my instruction, engages my students, and demonstrates to them how abstract concepts play out in the real world.
ex.t: 我发现，这样做让我的教学更有活力，让学生更投入，也向他们展示了抽象概念在现实世界中的实际运用。

ex.s: Best of all, my passion for my hobbies seems to inspire them to be passionate about finding their own.
ex.t: 最棒的是，我对爱好的热情似乎激励他们也热情地去寻找自己的爱好。

ex.s: My mum would find fun even when completing the most boring of tasks.
ex.t: 妈妈即使在完成最无聊的任务时也能找到乐趣。

ex.s: My dad and I were at a grocery store last evening.
ex.t: 当收银员扫描完所有商品后，爸爸伸手去拿钱包，却愣住了。

ex.s: When the cashier rang everything up, my dad reached for his wallet and froze.
ex.t: 当收银员把所有东西扫码结算后，我爸爸伸手去拿钱包，却愣住了。

ex.s: After we had twins and became a family of five, my husband and I decided to move from London back to Yorkshire, to be closer to my parents.
ex.t: 在有了双胞胎、成为一个五口之家后，我和丈夫决定从伦敦搬回约克郡，以便离我的父母更近。

ex.s: Packing up my parents’ house felt like a massive goodbye — that bedroom, those memories, the feeling of safety and shelter I always felt there.
ex.t: 收拾父母家的房子感觉像一场盛大的告别——那间卧室、那些记忆、我在那里始终感到的安全和庇护。

ex.s: Even though I’m a grown woman in my 40s with my own family, it felt scary not to have “home” to go back to.
ex.t: 尽管我已是个40多岁、有自己的家庭的成年女性，没有“家”可以回让我感到害怕。

ex.s: There was a silence as Dad continued to drink his tea, and I held my breath.
ex.t: 当爸爸继续喝他的茶时，一阵沉默，我屏住了呼吸。

ex.s: Sitting at the table, making my mini sandwich, I realised I was ready for our next chapter.
ex.t: 坐在桌前做我的迷你三明治时，我意识到我已经为我们的下一个篇章做好了准备。

ex.s: More than once, I found myself wondering just how my students, who’d created these people, knew their subjects so well.
ex.t: 不止一次，我发现自己想知道，创造了这些角色的我的学生们，怎么会如此了解他们所写的人物。

ex.s: The students took on diverse topics and turned in stories, 10 to 20 pages each, with characters that broadened my view and touched my heart.
ex.t: 学生们选择了各种不同的主题，交上来的故事每篇10到20页，其中的人物开阔了我的视野，也触动了我的心。

ex.s: However, my students demonstrated something more important to me.
ex.t: 那个男人慌忙站起来，然后穿过屋子朝窗户跑去，跳了出去。

ex.s: One August afternoon, I sat in my kitchen staring at a glass vase that hadn’t seen daylight since my wedding.
ex.t: 八月的一个下午，我坐在厨房里，盯着一只自婚礼以来就没再见天日的玻璃花瓶。

ex.s: Maybe you won’t.” In an instant, a woman raced into my house and left happily with the vase.
ex.t: “也许你不会要。”顷刻间，一位女士冲进我家，高高兴兴地拿着花瓶离开了。

ex.s: My wife and I wanted to share our new home with family and friends by hosting a small gathering in the early summer.
ex.t: 我和妻子想在初夏举办一个小聚会，与亲友分享我们的新家。

ex.s: She had prepared lots of snacks, while my job was to have the backyard in order.
ex.t: 社会比较会使我们陷入情绪困扰

ex.s: There was just one thing I hadn’t counted on: My brother chose to bring his dog Toby, a 50-pound ball of fire.
ex.t: 只有一件事我没料到：我弟弟选择带上他的狗Toby——一个50磅重的小火球。

ex.s: Though friendly, he could easily knock over my niece’s small boys and my six-month-old granddaughter.
ex.t: 虽然他很友善，但他很容易撞倒我侄女的小男孩和我六个月大的孙女。

ex.s: So, when my brother showed up, I asked him to watch Toby and keep him outside.
ex.t: 多年来，心理学家将身份认同看作是某人的价值观、信念、目标和社会角色的组合。

ex.s: My plan was working out just fine.
ex.t: 它们用鼻子来评估环境并留意任何危险的迹象。

ex.s: I didn’t want Toby to be running around in the house, and my brother wasn’t happy with driving home with a wet dog.
ex.t: 我不想让Toby在屋里乱跑，而我弟弟也不乐意开着车带着一只湿漉漉的狗回家。

ex.s: Eventually, my brother decided to leave rather than force the issue.
ex.t: 最终，我弟弟决定离开，而不是强求。

ex.s: My wife suggested I get in touch with my brother, but I resisted, thinking he should call first.
ex.t: 我妻子建议我和我弟弟取得联系，但我抗拒，觉得应该他先打电话。

ex.s: I tried to put myself in my brother’s shoes.
ex.t: 我试着把自己放在我哥哥的鞋子里。

ex.s: With the biscuits my wife had made, I arrived at my brother’s door.
ex.t: 带着我妻子做的饼干，我来到了我兄弟的家门口。

ex.s: Every time I gave a self-introduction, I had to explain how to pronounce my name at least five times, yet they still could not say it the way I did.
ex.t: 每次我作自我介绍时，都不得不把我的名字怎么读解释至少五遍，可他们还是说不出我那种读法。

ex.s: Once in a lecture, the professor tried repeating my name after me over and over in front of thirty classmates.
ex.t: 有一次在课上，教授当着三十名同学的面，一遍又一遍地跟着我重复我的名字。

ex.s: I feared that my classmates might grow tired of my efforts or even lose patience with me.
ex.t: 我担心同学们可能会厌倦我的努力，甚至对我失去耐心。

ex.s: However, I soon found that by doing so, I might be losing something more important: the opportunity to share a small part of my cultural identity.
ex.t: 然而我很快发现，这样做我可能正在失去更重要的东西：分享自己文化身份一小部分的机会。

ex.s: In a class discussion, I was invited to explain the meaning of my name.
ex.t: 在一次课堂讨论中，我被邀请解释我名字的含义。

ex.s: Many of my classmates got interested and came up to me after class.
ex.t: 我的许多同学产生了兴趣，课后围到我身边。

ex.t: “你不想变胖”这句话在我整个童年里被不断重复。

ex.t: 在校长办公室里，父亲专注地听着，然后以沉静的威严说道：“我相信我的儿子。”

ex.t: 多数放学后，我喜欢和我的狗尼克在森林里散步。

ex.s: Throughout our Junior year, my classmates and I have been worried about what colleges will see when they look at our whole life story reduced to a single 200-word essay.
ex.t: 整个高三那年，我和同学们一直担心，当大学招生官把我们整个生平浓缩成一篇200词的短文来审视时，他们会看到什么。

ex.s: My first step of redefining success began with course registrations.
ex.t: 我重新定义成功的第一步始于课程注册。

ex.s: It is a well-known fact, especially in my school, that Junior year is the time of packing many AP classes into the schedule.
ex.t: 这是一个众所周知的事实，尤其在我学校：高三是要把许多AP课程塞进课表的一年。

ex.s: When asked why they chose so many AP classes, my friends responded: “I don’t know.” They themselves don’t know why they are following the crowd and longing for the pressures of academic difficulty.
ex.t: 当被问及为什么选择这么多AP课程时，我的朋友们回答说：“我不知道。”他们自己也不知道为什么要随大流，为什么渴望学业压力。

ex.s: In the ninth grade, I went in for my first group interview for a leadership position as a shy girl.
ex.t: 九年级时，作为一个害羞的女孩，我参加了第一次为领导岗位而设的小组面试。

ex.s: Although my daughter didn’t win, she did help expose one of the worst pieces of advice I have ever given.
ex.t: 尽管我女儿没有赢，但她确实帮我暴露了我曾给过的最糟糕的建议之一。

ex.s: In my defence, I did what we’ve all done before, which is to repeat received wisdom without exploring the nuances.
ex.t: 为我自己辩护一下，我做了我们所有人都做过的事，那就是在不探究细节的情况下重复人云亦云的观点。

ex.s: What I wish I taught my daughter earlier are these nuances.
ex.t: 我希望更早教给我女儿的是这些细微差别。

ex.t: "我不喜欢这个结局，"我对我最喜欢的大学教授说。

ex.t: 我的手机在屋里，但幸好街对面有个电话亭。

ex.s: If I ever get trapped outside my house again, my local telephone box will, sadly, no longer be able to connect me with my keys.
ex.t: 如果我再被锁在屋外，可悲的是，我家附近的电话亭将不再能帮我联系到钥匙了。

ex.s: But it can certainly keep me entertained while I wait for my wife to rescue me.
ex.t: 但它肯定能在我等妻子来解救我的时候让我保持愉悦。

ex.t: 他还为位于中国东南部的福州市设计了一台生态机器来净化运河水。

ex.s: I wasn't going to let a grade stop me from learning some of the best lessons of my life.
ex.t: 我不会让一个年级 阻止我学习一些 我生命中最好的教训。

ex.t: 盯着书房里塞满了许多本一直未读的好书的书架，我脑海里响起一个响亮的声音——「你真丢人！」

ex.s: Clearly, my way of reading the text had shifted, and I myself had changed over the years.
ex.t: 显然，我阅读文本的方式已经改变，而这些年来我自己也变了。

ex.s: I read both definitions over again, trying to figure it out, but Miss Chevalier must have read my mind.

ex.t: 她说我妈妈在那点上说得有些对。

ex.t: 祖母从椅子上的短暂小睡中醒来，手指捋过波浪般的白发，望向窗外蓝天，问我如果只有一个愿望，我会许什么愿。

ex.s: My grandmother was born in Ireland.
ex.t: 我的祖母出生在爱尔兰。

ex.s: At 28, my grandmother walked herself through the snow to birth her first child.
ex.t: 28岁时，我的祖母独自踏着雪去生下她的第一个孩子。

ex.s: If I asked what she had for lunch, she might say, “Oh, the weather has been lovely today. ” She seemed to recycle the same handful of answers to my questions.
ex.t: 如果我问她午饭吃了什么，她可能会说："哦，今天天气真好。"她似乎总在用同样那几个答案应付我的问题。

ex.s: I must have always known reading was very important because the first memories I have as a child deal with books． There was not one night that I don't remember mom reading me a storybook by my bedside． I was extremely inspired by the elegant way the words sounded．
ex.t: 我一定一直都知道阅读非常重要，因为我童年最早的记忆都与书有关。没有哪个夜晚我不记得妈妈在床边给我读故事书。那些文字优雅的读音极大地启发了我。

ex.s: I always wanted to know what my mom was reading． Hearing mom say，"I can't believe what's printed in the newspaper this morning，" made me want to grab it out of her hands and read it myself． I wanted to be like my mom and know all of the things she knew． So I carried around a book， and each night， just to be like her， I would pretend to be reading．
ex.t: 我一直想知道妈妈在读什么。听到妈妈说“真不敢相信今天早上报纸上印了什么”，我就想从她手里抢过报纸自己读。我想成为像妈妈那样的人，知道她知道的所有事情。于是我随身带着一本书，每天晚上，就为了像她一样，我还会假装在阅读。

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: 每个人都是这样学会阅读的。我们从句子开始，然后是段落，再然后是故事。这似乎是一段永无止境的旅程，但即使作为一个六岁的女孩，我也意识到学会阅读能打开许多扇门。当妈妈说：“C-A-N-D-Y藏在最上面的架子上”时，我知道糖果在哪里。我在阅读上的进步激发了我的好奇心，我想知道一切。我经常叫妈妈开慢一点，这样我就能读出我们路过的所有路标。

ex.s: Most of my reading through primary， middle and high school was factual reading． I read for knowledge， and to make A's on my tests． Occasionally， I would read a novel that was assigned， but I didn't enjoy this type of reading． I liked facts， things that are concrete． I thought anything abstract left too much room for argument．
ex.t: 在小学、初中和高中阶段，我的大部分阅读都是事实性阅读。我为获取知识而读，为了在考试中拿A。偶尔，我也会读老师指定的小说，但我并不喜欢这种阅读。我喜欢事实，喜欢具体的东西。我认为任何抽象的事物都留下了太多争论的空间。

ex.s: We're taught to read because it's necessary for much of human understanding． Reading is a vital part of my life． Reading satisfies my desire to keep learning． And I've found that the possibilities that lie within books are limitless．
ex.t: 我们被教导阅读，因为这对于人类理解的许多内容来说是必要的。阅读是我生活中不可或缺的一部分。阅读满足了我不断学习的渴望。而且我发现，书中蕴含的可能性是无限的。
